summary: Interrogated the PH-5 draft against the roadmap story's five acceptance criteria, the confirmed project-record spec, every active decision ID, and the read-only exploration of the seams. Every task traces to a criterion. Three findings resolved into the plan before saving; the plan makes no new decisions because every choice derives from the confirmed spec or an existing record, which was checked against each active ID.
gaps: AC5's guard was drafted as a check in roadmap.py. That risked validating at load, which PH-2's lesson (and decision 0021's authoring-not-loading rule) says breaks legacy roadmaps — a client roadmap predating the marker would fail to load.

The plan asserted recording in the planning-lock hook 'authorizes nothing' without pinning why. The guard flow (pre_tool_use.py:221) was read: the early return at :231 fires before the quickfix check, so recording must be inserted before it; recording appends to the window's file list and reaches no deny and returns nothing, so no authorization path is added. Verified, not assumed.

The PR-link home could have been run.json's --pr-url, which already exists. Exploration proved pr_ready.py:332 reduces run.json to {project, phase} at ship, destroying it — so the event ledger is the only home that survives, which is what the spec already chose.
resolutions: AC5 guard moved from roadmap.py (load-time) to forge doctor (a report). pr_ready already requires an outcome to ship, so a new story cannot become outcome-less; doctor names the historical unmarked case without gating legacy loads. Task-4 scope and Surface Impact updated to doctor.py.

The recording seam is documented as append-only before the approved-plan early return, with claim_files (the budget) unchanged on the authorization path — the spec's separation of recording from bounding, verified against the actual guard flow. A test asserts the lock still refuses an unbudgeted write.
PR link stays an event (spec's one home), confirmed against pr_ready's run.json projection which would erase any run-state field.
open_items: roadmap.json remains a single mutable file that has lost items to merges twice. Named in the plan's Non-goals as a separate decision (making it conflict-free like the 0022 ledgers), not resolved in this story — it is real but distinct from record completeness.
Decision 0025's brief-durability question (what a worker was told, no longer committed) is parked from the spec grill and stays out of scope here.
